content: Intravenous prostaglandin E2 and F2 alpha can be utilized to induce labor, but their application is restricted due to the unacceptable side-effect profiles observed in mothers. These side effects have limited their widespread use in clinical practice. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effects of intravenous prostaglandin on cervical ripening or labor induction during the third trimester of pregnancy. The review included randomized controlled trials that compared intravenous prostaglandin with either placebo, no treatment, or other predefined methods of labor induction. A total of thirteen trials involving 1,165 women were included in the analysis. The findings revealed that the use of intravenous prostaglandin was associated with significantly higher rates of uterine hyperstimulation. This hyperstimulation occurred both with changes in fetal heart rate (relative risk [RR] 6.76, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.23 to 37.11) and without changes in fetal heart rate (RR 4.25, 95% CI 1.48 to 12.24) when compared to oxytocin. Additionally, the use of intravenous prostaglandin was linked to a significantly higher incidence of maternal side effects, including gastrointestinal disturbances, thrombophlebitis, and fever (RR 3.75, 95% CI 2.46 to 5.70), compared to oxytocin. However, prostaglandin was not found to be more effective than oxytocin in achieving vaginal delivery (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.61 to 1.18). Subgroup analyses and comparisons of combination therapies, such as prostaglandin F2 alpha with oxytocin or extra-amniotic prostaglandin E2 with intravenous prostaglandin E2, did not reveal any significant differences in outcomes. In conclusion, intravenous prostaglandin does not demonstrate superior efficacy compared to intravenous oxytocin for labor induction. However, its use is associated with a higher risk of maternal side effects and uterine hyperstimulation. No definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding the efficacy of combining prostaglandin F2 alpha with oxytocin or comparing extra-amniotic prostaglandin E2 with intravenous prostaglandin E2. It is also noted that two citations awaiting classification may potentially influence the conclusions of this review once they are assessed.
